issues.legal_issue: A plaintiff seeking a declaration of rights to land must prove the basis of the claim, and the opposing party’s failure to prove its allegations does not shift that burden.
material_facts: The plaintiffs claimed rights based on an oral grant of a tenancy, but did not state when the grant was made or produce receipts for land revenue or crop payments.

The plaintiffs produced revenue entries for some plots from 1950 to 1952, when the land had admittedly been allotted to the plaintiff’s father for one year; later entries recorded the land as part of an industrial area in favour of the State’s Commercial Department.
The plaintiffs’ names appeared in the revenue record as encroachers, and the State had declared them encroachers in 1978.

The trial court and first appellate court dismissed the suit, but the High Court reversed those concurrent decisions, reasoning in part that the State had not produced original revenue entries and had not proved the plaintiffs’ possession was that of encroachers.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred by placing the burden of proving the plaintiffs’ title and possession on the State. The Supreme Court set aside the High Court’s judgment and restored the concurrent dismissal of the suit.
issues.legal_principle: A plaintiff seeking relief must prove the plaintiff’s own case; the defendant’s failure to prove an allegation does not relieve the plaintiff of that burden. The Supreme Court cited no earlier case or specific statutory provision for this principle.

predicates.civil_land_title_suit: The proceeding is a civil suit in which a plaintiff claims rights to land.
predicates.second_appeal_reverses_concurrent_dismis: A second appellate court reverses concurrent decisions dismissing the plaintiff’s suit.
predicates.plaintiff_claimed_title_without_identify: The plaintiff relied on an alleged oral grant but did not identify when it was made.
predicates.claimant_lacked_supporting_revenue_or_cr: The claimant did not produce receipts supporting the claimed landholding or payments to the alleged grantor.
predicates.appellate_court_shifted_burden_to_defend: The appellate court relied on the defendant’s failure to prove its allegations rather than requiring the plaintiff to prove the plaintiff’s claim.
predicates.second_appeal_reversal_is_set_aside: The reversal of the concurrent dismissals is set aside.

issues.definition: When a land-title plaintiff leaves the claimed oral grant and supporting payments unsubstantiated, an appellate reversal of concurrent dismissals based on shifting the burden to the defendant is set aside.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant relying on adverse possession must disclose and prove when the adverse possession began and when it became complete.
material_facts: The plaintiffs amended their plaint to plead adverse possession after losing in the trial court in the first round of proceedings.
They did not establish when their alleged adverse possession began or when it became complete.
The Tehsildar had declared the plaintiffs encroachers in 1978.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiffs failed to prove their adverse-possession claim.
issues.legal_principle: A party pleading adverse possession must disclose and prove when the possession became adverse and when the required period of possession was completed. The court particularly noted the prior declaration that the plaintiffs were encroachers. No earlier case or specific statutory provision was cited for this principle.

predicates.civil_land_title_suit: The proceeding is a civil suit in which a plaintiff claims rights to land.
predicates.claimant_relies_on_adverse_possession: The claimant relies on adverse possession as a basis for acquiring rights to land.
predicates.claimant_did_not_prove_start_of_adverse_: The claimant did not prove when the possession became adverse.
predicates.claimant_did_not_prove_completion_of_adv: The claimant did not prove when the adverse possession became complete.

issues.definition: An adverse-possession claim fails when a land claimant does not prove when the possession became adverse and when it became complete, particularly where the claimant had been declared an encroacher.
